recommended_by_category.title: Taking Street Fighter Worldwide!
recommended_by_category.author: sf6team
recommended_by_category.body: Hello everyone, this is the localization director for Street Fighter 6! Localization’s main job is to translate from Japanese to other languages, but we also have the responsibility of translating both words and meaning for players around the world. We also write voiceover scripts in English and record them. September is when Fatal Fury’s Terry Bogard makes his way into Street Fighter 6, so I wanted to talk about how we handled his character! First, because Terry is the pride of SNK, we met with SNK’s localization team and gave them ideas on how we wanted to write his character. We already knew about their upcoming Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves, but the Terry that appears in Street Fighter 6 is from before that time, so to give him more personality, we wanted to place his speech pattern around the 1980s-1990s, when Terry first appeared. This means he doesn’t speak like Luke, who’s younger and from a newer generation. Instead, Terry says “rad” instead of “awesome”, “from downtown” instead of “from long range”, and “groovy” instead of “cool”. We also gave other characters who show up in the update, such as Blue Mary and Joe Higashi their own unique speaking style to make them sound more like the games they came from. Terry has rarely had English voice acting in the past, with Street Fighter 6 we were fortunate enough to call on the same voice actor as Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves. Because the voice actor was already familiar with the character, we worked together to change his lines during recording if he wanted to try something different. We hope that we can give you a great alternative to the already great Japanese voice acting! Speaking of that, the Street Fighter team was kind enough to ask me to write the original Japanese battle script for Terry. Because Terry speaks a lot of English during his attacks, they felt it would be cooler if an English speaker wrote his battle script. It was fun, but a little difficult since I had to write everything in both English and katakana! It took twice as long to write everything because of the katakana! Also coming out with the Terry update is the new V-Rival mode that can be found in the Battle Hub. While the V-Rival name is the same in all languages, the name for Li-Fen’s cute panda assistant was localized. In Japanese, its name is Manemon-kun, which comes from the Japanese word to mimic something. In English and other languages, because the V-Rival machine is a panda, we decided to go with Sim Sim, which sounds like a Panda’s name, and is also short for Simulation! That’s all I have for today! Street Fighter 6 is a truly global title with casual and pro players from around the world. It’s important that our fans can not only play the game but have entertaining stories to experience, and easy to understand tutorials, and that’s one of localization’s most important responsibilities. I hope we achieved that with this game! ---------------- Written by Canadian Destroyer - Localization Director A Canadian who loves fighting games. I take care of translation, voice direction and much more! ----------------

recommended_by_category.title: Lighting M. Bison's Super Arts
recommended_by_category.author: Guest
recommended_by_category.body: Hello there, everyone! Lighting team here! Today, we'd like to talk a bit about what went into lighting M. Bison's Super Arts animations! Every frame in a game like this matters, so we work very hard to make sure every frame the players see is beautiful. These are animations that people will be seeing over and over, so we watch them hundreds of times to make sure they never get dull. Lighting isn't just about the lights themselves, however. We also work closely with the effects team to add things like smoke or adjust lens focus to make sure the visuals work. Our goal for Super Arts is to make sure the beautiful models and fantastic animations are able to really shine to their fullest potential. When we really want the player to focus on a certain aspect of an animation, we do a number of things to draw the eye, like adjusting the depth of field by altering lens focus, using contrasting brightness in lighting, or emphasizing an area by giving it extra lighting. We also want to leave the biggest impact as possible on the player, so we further emphasize by highlighting the tempo of the animation by increasing the overall lighting as the animation with each hit or as time passes. Let's look at a few examples of what we're talking about with a M. Bison's Super Arts! Super Art 1 (Knee Press Nightmare) M. Bison's level 1 Super Art is quite short, so we adjusted the coloring of the lights to make the character stand out. We also made some adjustments in order to draw the eye to Bison's throat slit motion at the beginning of the animation. It was difficult to keep Bison shadowy and dark like he should be, while also helping him stand out enough. Super Art 2 Psycho Punisher Bison's level 2 Super Art includes a bit of camera work, which requires more of a heavy hand when it comes to lighting adjustments. We've tried to draw the eye to Bison's legs with the lighting to emphasize the power of his legs as he readies to launch himself in the air. We also wanted to bring attention to his cape, so we've set a light just for that purpose. Super Art 3/Critical Art (Unlimited Psycho Crusher) The Super Art level 3/Critical Art has all kind of lighting adjustments in order to make it look as cool as possible. This makes what we're doing a little bit more obvious. In addition to the light from the Psycho Power in M. Bison's hands, you've got big movements in his spins and flip, so we wanted to make sure those movements were as easy to see as possible while detailing the effects around Bison's arms in a satisfying way. Having the light spin along with Bison during the animation only serves to overwhelm the player's senses, so we decided to keep the light stationary. For the flash resulting from the final explosion, we worked closely with the effects team to have the flash come not when the explosion begins expanding, but when it's close to its full expansion. This gives the whole animation a snappier feel to it. And that's all we have for today! Lights appear all over the game outside of just Super Arts. Entrance animations, victory animations, World Tour cutscenes... We light them all to make sure each frame can reach its full potential. Every placement and color adjustment is made in hopes to amplify the characterization of each individual character while also ensuring that the style is consistent over the whole game. We hope we achieved this with all the Year 1 characters and M. Bison too! We hope you'll look forward to future characters as well! Until next time!

recommended_by_category.title: Introducing Outfit 3 by the design team!
recommended_by_category.author: Guest
recommended_by_category.body:
We’ve seen all your comments and Outfit 3 for the 18 launch characters is finally coming to Street Fighter 6! When we revealed the first four at Evo 2023 back in August, we were blown away at the reaction, especially since we put so much of our love of the series into each outfit. Our design team wanted to provide their comments on the inspiration, story, and elements of each outfit. Read on to learn more!

Kimberly

Design Team: At first, I struggled to find the right direction, but with the help of those around me, I was able to give form to Kimberly's idea of what she enthusiastically thinks is "ninja-like." I am very honored to have been in charge of designing this outfit, as she is one of my favorite characters. I love her cute round hair and round pants and I hope you try her out in-game!

Jamie

Design Team: His everyday clothes are casual, but he comes out swinging when he has to. The concept of him wearing formal Chinese clothes was decided at an early stage and his politeness and upbringing from his grandmother/master is conveyed through this outfit. Arranging and decorating this outfit too much would make it feel out of place, and simplifying too much would lack in character, so it took a long time to find the right balance with the help of our Chinese staff.

JP

Design Team: At first, I aimed for a more western style, like a black robe, but landed on this design because we thought it would be nice to have a Nayshall outfit referencing the storyline. I also wanted to see an older gentleman fight in a traditional garb, and felt it would be a shame to not show some skin since he is such a big-framed character.

Chun-Li

Design Team: The concept of this outfit is Chun-Li's casual wear. I thought that even her casual clothes would maintain an ease of movement and elegance, so I combined inner-wear that combines aspects of training attire with a Chinese-influenced jacket. The large slit shows her back when she moves, and the transparency provides a delicate touch when seen on the screen. Her sweatpants were designed with a basketball jersey in mind with side buttons that can be undone at the waist to make it easier for a character with thick thighs like Chun-Li to put them on. I've also never seen Chun-Li wear wide-legged pants before, so I decided to give this a shot.

Ryu

Design Team: I was thinking of a situation of Ryu wearing normal clothes and felt he might dress a little more like a regular person when he comes down from the mountain where he trains to head to town. From there, I thought about what he does in town, and imagined him going to public baths, buying ingredients for his meals, and washing his gi before returning to the mountain. We came up with the idea of Chun-Li scolding Ryu for roaming around town with his gi on, so she decides to buy him a jacket. He is also wearing a towel wrapped around his head that he wears after taking a bath, brand-new bandages, jeans that have been washed so many times that the color has faded and looks like white denim, and high-end sandals that were gifted from E. Honda.

Manon

Design Team: I was asked to come up with the design for Manon's casual attire. The concept we landed on was a noble outfit inspired by the French Revolution. I had other concepts in mind like a ballet dancer costume, but after much trial and error, I finally settled on this outfit. I wanted to make the lower half of her body into a white horse, and make her into something like a centaur, but that idea was ultimately dismissed.

E. Honda

Design Team: This costume was inspired by the concept of vacationing on a tropical island. I've seen TV programs of Sumo wrestlers taking vacations during their off-season, which is where I came up with this idea. His fun and relaxed vibes and the shirt's impactful pattern and coloring were designed to stand out and leave a lasting impression. I think the design is aligned with E. Honda's respect for Japanese culture.

Dhalsim

Design Team: I have an image of Dhalsim caring for and wearing handmade items that have been gifted to him. He is surprisingly sociable, so I designed him as if you might see him in the middle of town, having tea with a friend.

Zangief

Design Team: I was asked for a design to show his unlikely intellectual side, and his dignified position as a wrestler. The design process went quite smoothly between the art director and me. I like the way his badge and watch make a strong statement.

Blanka

Design Team: This version of Blanka-chan, has been redesigned to differ from past iterations. Initially, I wanted to try something different, and at first considered a "Blanka as a working man" concept but ended up settling on this one. This design matches Blanka's Outfit 1.

Ken

Design Team: Ken has lost a lot in this game, so I wanted to show him looking sharp and stylish like the heir that he is. While each component of his outfit is fairly simple, I like to think that he's wearing extremely valuable material. Since he has his leather jacket zipped up, it might be a little difficult for him to move.

Lily

Design Team: This is Lily in her traditional Mexican outfit that she might wear at a local festival. I thought pants would be easier to move in, and would suit Lily's personality better than a dress, so I designed this outfit with the inspiration from a mariachi costume. While maintaining her refreshing and brave impression, I used items like a large sombrero, bright flower hair ornaments, and red ribbons to enhance her cuteness.

Cammy

Design Team: The red coat Cammy wore in the Street Fighter II movie was so striking that I designed her to wear a similar red coat that she might wear when going undercover. I designed the coat in a more modern and functional style that I thought would suit her. I also gave her a pendant to symbolize the bond with her allies.

Luke

Design Team: This outfit appeared in SFV but I actually came up with this after Luke's design for SF6 was established. The concept of this outfit was "more aggressive," and "young and cocky." The stars on his forearms are tattoos that he got every time he has won an underground martial arts tournament or an official tournament, and he eventually got them removed because he was embarrassed when he found out that his father had embroidered stars on his jacket for every comrade he couldn't save. My favorite part of this design are the braces on his teeth, which I hoped would express his immaturity and his ferociousness that look like as if he might come bite at you.

Dee Jay

Design Team: Design Team - For this game, I wanted to emphasize Dee Jay's artist aspect, so I designed this outfit thinking that he would have a great suit that would make any place turn into a dance hall whenever he had it on. His style is that he never forgets to be playful any chance he gets.

Juri

Design Team: This outfit was based on the idea of what she lounges around in at home. Her default outfit already gave a strong impression of what she might wear for her casual clothes, so we considered her off-duty state and landed on this design. I was careful not to dilute her aggressive and provocative aspects even when she is off duty. One of the things I want to highlight are her hair horns that become disheveled from sleeping in this outfit.

Marisa

Design Team: This is her wedding dress. She is a character full of confidence, so several ideas for a gorgeous party dress were originally proposed. However, since her expression of love is a strong character trait, I wanted to directly utilize that as a concept for her outfit. To emphasize the strength of the character, we created a silhouette that extends downwards, and settled on a goddess of war motif for the overall composition.

Guile

Design Team: I came up with this design starting with the concept of what Guile would look like if he worked at a bar in the countryside when he's off duty. He has strong, broad shoulders, so even if he's wearing a shirt with sleeves, I made it so it clearly shows the lines of his shoulders. The design on his back is because he used to be in the Air Force. I aimed to create a retro, everyday look that evokes a nostalgic aspect of Guile. That’s all we have for you today! What about Rashid and A.K.I.? Their Outfit 3s will arrive when Akuma releases next year. For now, we wanted to focus on the launch roster. We hope to see these outfits being worn online, as well as all the cosplay and fan art from all our amazing fans.

column.title: A Toast Between Fathers
column.author: Scenario Team
column.body:
With a loud squeak, the doors of the Metro City Pub creaked open, and a man in a suit came stumbling in.
 
The bartender, polishing glasses behind the counter, took a quick glance at the man. He was wearing a satin suit, with flowers still pinned to its glossy lapel—a rose, decorated with lavender. If the sway in the man’s step didn’t give away that this wasn’t his first drink of the evening, his disregard of the pub’s neon “Closed” sign almost certainly did.

“Two bourbons,” the man said, “one on the rocks, and another neat—no chaser.” Taking measure of the situation, the bartender gestured toward two seats at the counter, set out a couple of coasters, and got to work chipping ice. 

“Helluva wedding!”

“It certainly seems—”

“Your son turned out to be a fine man.” The bartender looked up, noticing that the man was facing the seat next to him. He cracked a small smile, and went quietly back to work. The man continued speaking in a warm, intimate tenor.

“You know, when I first met your boy, I could still hold Patricia in one arm. He was just like you—spit an’ vinegar, always making enemies and trying to play the tough guy.” The man swung his head and laughed. “Didn’t stop his soft side from leaking through, though.”

“You should’ve seen him the first time I let him hold Patricia. Had no idea what to do. He’d spent so long learning to fight people bigger and stronger than him that he was totally lost on how to handle something so small and helpless. So I decides to tease him a bit, yeah? ‘Hey!’ I say, ‘You better not fight with her, you hear?’ And you know what he said to me? ‘Nah, then I’d be a bully. Dad said to never be a bully...”

“‘That so?’ I says, ‘and what if someone else tries to bully her, huh?’ He whipped his neck around, looked me straight in the eye, and said ‘I’ll make ‘em wish they hadn’t.’ Hoo boy, that gaze shot through me like bullet.”

The man’s story was interrupted by the gentle clinking of ice hitting glass, indicating the drinks were ready. The bartender held out the first glass for the man to take, and set the other on the coaster next to him.

“Cheers,” the man said, and the bartender went about his work behind the counter.

“Patricia wanted to be just like him. Always following him around, begging for attention. It worried me, if I’m being honest. Much as I loved Alex, he’s not exactly a perfect role model. But honestly, I think it took him a bit off guard. He kept his distance, never getting in her way but also making sure she never got hurt. He followed through on his word—reliable, just like his pops! Gwahaha!”

“Anyways, at one point or another, he must’ve gotten sick of me. Typical teenager, desperate for independence. Especially your boy. Around the time he went to high school, I scrounged up enough cash to buy him an old pickup. He poured his soul into that piece of junk. Worked on it every day, too. Hell, he even slept in it more often than not.”

The man paused, took a swig of his drink, and continued.

“I...I wasn’t always there for Patricia, you know. Hell, of course you do—after the divorce and all...things took a real turn for the worse.” He turned to the seat next to him and continued. “She got herself into some real trouble. Always coming home late, doing as she pleased, getting involved with the wrong kinda people. One day, she didn’t come home. That’s when he—”

The man trailed off, and a pained expression crept across his face.

“When Alex found out, he was having none of it. After some yelling, he roughed up a few guys, found out where Patricia was taken, and brought her back home. Left a reeeal path of destruction behind him.”

The man’s knuckles turned white around his glass, and his other hand clenched into a fist.

“I...I should’ve done something. I know I should’ve done something. I just... I didn’t want to get in her way, you know? But Alex...”

The man’s grip slackened.

“Alex, man... He did what I couldn’t. Even though they’d grown apart, he was there when she needed him.”

The man’s eyes took on a shiny gloss, and he let out a nervous laugh.

“She’s lucky to have him. You hear that? You got two troublemakers now, and I have a son—the best son in the world!”

The man turned around as if to speak to the whole pub.

“You all hear that!? I’ve got the best son-in-law in the world! What more could a father ask for!”

“...Helluva wedding, buddy. I sure hope you were watching.”

The man lowered his head and spoke in a hushed voice, then clinked his glass against the one next to him as if to toast.

“To our new family!”

In one quick motion, the man pulled his head back and emptied the rest of his drink. Eyes closed, he took a deep, quivering breath, then stood up to pay. The bartender just shook his head.

“The drinks are on the house, sir. Congratulations. To the both of you.”

“Mighty fine of you!”

The man made it half way to the door, then stopped for a moment as if remembering something. Turning around, he walked back to the seat beside his and plopped the flowers from his lapel into the still-full glass of bourbon.

By the time the man finally took his leave, the bar had opened, and people began trickling in. Hushed conversations gradually stirred to a din of lively banter and laughter as the pub filled. When someone would approach the counter to sit, the bartender would turn them away.

“Sorry,” he’d say, “this seat’s taken,” and he’d gesture towards the flowers—rose, decorated with lavender.

The counter stayed empty through the night.

index.[t]description: Info on the latest iteration of the Street Fighter series!
index.[t]concept__text:
A new era for fighting games begins in 2023!
The evolution of fighting games starts with our traditional Fighting Ground,
and then we're turning the genre on its head with World Tour and Battle Hub for a total of three modes where anyone can play to their liking.
No one starts off as a champion. You get there step by step, punch by punch.
Take up the challenge and bring your game to the next level.
